assumptions: Argumentative passages can be reworded into numbered propositions without loss of the reasoning at issue.
Validity is a matter of logical form, so an argument's merit can be separated from the truth of its content.
Suppressed premises can be reconstructed and fairly attributed to the person who advanced the argument.
Ordinary English must be understood by a reader rather than translated by mechanical rules.
Probabilities for uncertain future outcomes can at least be estimated, enabling comparison of risky decisions.
limitations: Validity alone does not establish that an argument's premises or conclusion are true.
Because their conclusions are never certain, the terms validity and invalidity do not apply to inductive arguments.
Symbolization depends on the interpreter's grasp of meaning; no formal or mechanical rules govern translation from English.
Diagramming risks inserting more information into the diagram than the premises warrant.
Stipulative definitions can be useful or useless but cannot resolve genuine disagreements.
The evidence sample is a selection of pages, so coverage of the full book is incomplete.
not_for: Designing empirical studies or choosing statistical tests
Settling questions of metalogic or mathematical foundations beyond the textbook scope
Proving mathematical theorems at research level
Replacing domain expertise in medicine, engineering, or economics
Formal verification of software or hardware systems

frameworks.name: Deductive Validity Test
frameworks.one_liner: Determines by form alone whether an argument's premises could be true while its conclusion is false, using Venn diagrams or truth tables.
applicable_when: A conclusion is claimed to follow with necessity
A syllogism, conditional argument, or chain of rule-governed steps must be checked
A proposed counterexample would show invalidity
failure_modes: Concluding that a valid argument has a true conclusion when its premises are false
Applying the validity-accuracy vocabulary to an inductive argument, where it does not apply
Misplacing diagram marks and thereby inserting information the premises do not warrant
Treating a truth-functionally material conditional as a causal or evidential one

frameworks.name: Definition Stress Test
frameworks.one_liner: Evaluates a proposed definition against the rules of genus and difference and asks whether it can settle or only restate the dispute.
applicable_when: Two parties argue past each other because a key term is unclear
A stipulative definition is offered to end a debate
A legal or philosophical definition must be checked for scope
failure_modes: Rejecting a stipulative definition for being untrue when it is only a proposal
Accepting a definition that is unclear but rhetorically convenient
Assuming an agreed definition settles a substantive disagreement it only redescribes

frameworks.name: Enthymeme Reconstruction
frameworks.one_liner: Recovers the unstated premises of a persuasive argument and tests whether the conclusion actually follows once they are supplied.
applicable_when: The argument's conclusion depends on a plausible but unstated second premise
A policy or legal claim is urged rhetorically rather than demonstrated
Two sides disagree without stating what exactly they disagree about
failure_modes: Supplying a premise stronger than the proponent would accept, thereby building in a straw man
Supplying a premise so weak the conclusion still does not follow, then declaring the argument sound
Treating the reconstructed premise as if the proponent had asserted it
Collapsing the difference between a plausible premise and a true one

frameworks.name: Expectation-Value Decision Frame
frameworks.one_liner: Compares chancy alternatives by multiplying each outcome's return by its probability and summing the products.
applicable_when: Investments, wagers, or policy options have enumerable outcomes
Probabilities can at least be estimated even though the future is unknown
Two or more risky options must be ranked on a common scale
failure_modes: Treating estimated probabilities as known facts
Ignoring outcomes that are hard to quantify
Comparing options whose returns are measured on incompatible scales
Letting a higher expectation value override a catastrophic low-probability outcome without discussion

frameworks.name: Fallacy Audit with Contextual Exception
frameworks.one_liner: Screens an argument for relevance, ambiguity, and assumption defects while testing whether a special context licenses an otherwise fallacious move.
applicable_when: A claim is advanced through a loaded question, a clipped quotation, or an attack on the speaker
A courtroom, legislative, or journalistic setting supplies agreed-upon rules of evidence
A rhetorical question needs its buried premise exposed
failure_modes: Charging ad hominem whenever a speaker's credibility is questioned, even where testimony is at issue
Calling a complex question fallacious while ignoring that some of its parts are uncontroversial
Treating a clipped quotation as a mere stylistic quibble rather than a reversal of sense
Applying courtroom standards of evidence to informal polemic, or vice versa

frameworks.name: Inductive Causal Appraisal
frameworks.one_liner: Weighs a causal or predictive claim by the inductive method used to support it and states the probability level it actually earns.
applicable_when: A policy or medical claim rests on observed regularities
Concomitant variation, method of difference, or analogy is doing the causal work
A conclusion is offered with more certainty than the evidence carries
failure_modes: Reporting a correlation as an established causal connection
Using the vocabulary of validity and invalidity for an inductive conclusion
Over-generalizing from a voluntary or unrepresentative sample
Ignoring that the same data admit a weaker as well as a stronger reading

frameworks.name: Refutation by Logical Analogy
frameworks.one_liner: Attacks a non-deductive argument by constructing a different argument of the same form whose conclusion is known or widely believed to be false.
applicable_when: The target argument is scientific, political, or economic rather than deductively claimed
Its form is recognizable but its conclusion seems intuitively right
A counterexample must be shown without disputing every premise
failure_modes: Choosing a refuting analogy whose form differs subtly from the target
Assuming the target is deductive, where a same-form counterexample shows only false premises rather than invalidity
Failing to distinguish a form defect from an unlucky choice of content
Using the technique to dismiss an argument whose conclusion is independently well supported

frameworks.name: Two-Dimensional Argument Diagram
frameworks.one_liner: Numbers every proposition in a complex passage and draws its premise-to-conclusion relations graphically to expose structure and gaps.
applicable_when: Several arguments are interwoven in one passage
Conclusions of subarguments serve as premises for further arguments
An extended chain of reasoning must be checked step by step
failure_modes: Adding information the passage does not assert
Assuming an arrow because two propositions are topically related
Over-reading a passage whose connectives are ambiguous
Producing a diagram too intricate to communicate to a reader
